posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
Wow, Ron, You work fast. How are you electrically isolating everything in the resonator?

![Image](http://www.rotorwave.com/hyosc7.jpg)

posts.author: Ron Michael
posts.content_md: cavity is pvc insulated from resonator and resonator is rubber gromment/nylon bolt isolated from chassis. eventually Pvc covers will be place over the anode/cathode terminals and covers placed over Hv components of the powersupply.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: I just read throught the latest update. Nice work! Instead of replacing the YAG rod for the resonator have you considered my idea of placing a telescope in the cavity? Since the aperture has to be small for the difraction losses a 4 to 1 telescope would improve the energy extraction from the rod.

posts.author: Ron Michael
posts.content_md: no, the 4 inch yag rod is fine, I'm manipulating the saturable absorber q switch parameters in the oscillator. If you use the telescope idea, remember the rod initially goes negative lensing during q switch time on low rep rate. So you need to tune for that. The pumping spectral tests show I should get enough energy in the limited diffraction volume of a conventional design, plus I'm trying to avoid the larger radius depolarization issues by keeping the beam small in the center.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
> **Ron Michael:** plus I'm trying to avoid the larger radius depolarization issues by keeping the beam small in the center.

I'll look into that. Thank you.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: How do you calculate the cavity efficiency? Would silver plating the cavity help? Who would provide a plating service?

posts.author: Ron Michael
posts.content_md: yes, protected silver doesn't have the small dip at 800nm like aluminum.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: Reading about it, you would need to polish the alluminum, nickle plate, polish the nickel plate, plate with silver, overcoat. It sounds expensive. Do you know of a company who can provide this service?

posts.author: Ron Michael
posts.content_md: No particular company comes to mind. I just polished the aluminum and up the joules. Since these lamps were running up to 10% explosion limit, it wasn't a real problem to increase power except the need to redesign power supplies, switch out caps.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: What wire is suitable for connecting to the flash lamps?

posts.author: Ron Michael
posts.content_md:
Get 18 guage 15kv wire. Check C and H electronic supply out in CA, I can get it if you can't. On big pulse ruby I use 12guage 15kv wire but that wouldn't be necessary for yag power levels. check the web for suppliers,

found this: [http://www.dearborn-cdt.com/catalog/HW-39-A-VP14.html](http://www.dearborn-cdt.com/catalog/HW-39-A-VP14.html)

posts.author: Ron Michael
posts.content_md: I can get the 40kv 18 guage wire if you need it. by the foot.

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md: How about gold plating? Would it be possible to cover the cavity with thin gold foil used for gold plating wooden ornaments? Or does that type of gold have a melting temperature that is too low?

posts.author: Ron Michael
posts.content_md: I have had aluminum foil melt before. My guess is it would melt. You need a thicker plating for the gold to last.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: The water cooled pulsed YAG's that I have seen have a gold plated housing interiour. I assume this is electroplated.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: Yes, Gold electroplating is common in YAG design. It helps get some of the pump energy that is lost in aluminum and Silver. It needs to be polished and it works better if it is vapor deposition and not electroplated.
